subject: english-language
title: Speech in the Wild
welcome_lead: How presenters, teachers and friends shape their speech.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on speech contexts and analysis.
final_note: You can now analyse a short transcript for speech features.

concepts.def: Stress, tone and rhythm of speech.

walkthroughs.body_html: A transcript writes down speech with pauses (…), overlaps and repairs. It shows messiness that polished writing hides.
Prosody covers stress, rhythm and intonation. A rising tone can turn a statement into a question.
Speakers adapt to context: classroom vs canteen, parent vs friend. Spotting context explains every choice in a transcript.

What is the difference between free and bound morphemes?
options: Free morphemes are free to use and bound morphemes cost money to use.
Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
Free morphemes can stand alone as words ('cat', 'happy', 'run'); bound morphemes must attach to another morpheme (prefixes, suffixes — 'un-', '-ness', '-ing').
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a dialect and an accent?
options: Accent refers only to pronunciation; dialect includes vocabulary and grammar as well as pronunciation — so all dialects involve accents but not vice versa.
Free morphemes are nouns and bound morphemes are verbs.
A dialect is a foreign language; an accent is how locals speak.
Dialect and accent mean the same thing.
